title: Đàn nguyệt (moon lute)
summary: The moon lute is a Vietnamese lute whose body is a perfectly round disc, like a full moon. It has a short neck with tall frets and two pairs of strings tuned a fifth apart. Its clear, glassy tone carries melodies in folk song and chamber music.
howToPlay: Two pairs of strings run up the neck, the lower pair on the left. Each lane marks the fret where a note is played.
A bead slides down the strings to its fret. Pluck the lane as the bead lands.
Notes high on the neck sit on the frets that run onto the round body.
Try the moonlit line first, then the bright run, then the answering pairs.
rules: The notes come from a five-note scale: G, A, C, D and E, in two octaves.
Every phrase is played through twice.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
The bright run has two beats to the bar; the others have four.
heritageNote: The moon lute has been played in Vietnam for many centuries and still accompanies song and small ensembles. Its round body is made from thin wood, and its tall frets let players bend and slide the notes of the folk scale.
